title: Introduction to Literature
description: A study of major literary works that introduces students to basic ideas and terminology in literary criticism. Students learn to read and interpret a selection of novels, plays, poetry, or other forms of writing to be determined each semester by the instructor.

title: American Dream
description: Utilizing the lens of literature and film, students will explore how the American Dream, understood as a broad, enduring, illusory, and contested narrative, has influenced creators worldwide. Themes of origins, access, home, landscape, community, and self-actualization will be examined as represented across various historical and cultural contexts within and beyond national borders. Engaging with a diverse selection of U.S. and diasporic voices prepares students to critically examine how narratives can shape both imaginations and nations.

title: Literature Studies
description: Independent study of selected readings in the field of literature, supervised by a faculty member.

title: Science and Fiction
description: An exploration of the ongoing dialogue between science/technology and literature through the reading of landmark works about science and fictional works that describe scientific ideas and methods. Topics include artificial intelligence, genetic engineering, and cyborgs.

title: Irish Literature
description: A survey of major works by Irish authors writing in English, with a particular focus on the fiction and drama of the twentieth century. Authors will include: Oscar Wilde, Samuel Beckett, James Joyce, and W.B. Yeats.

title: Film Theory
description: The purpose of this course is to study significant theories of representation that analyze the visual codifications generically called “film.” The course will examine theories of visual rhetoric and of narrativity; look at the way economic and technological factors have affected the construction of cinematic codes, styles, and trends; examine influential psychoanalytic theories and feminist theories; and consider the ways in which popular films participate in the cultural narratives specific to their moment of production.

title: 200 Year Old Vampires – Reflecting on Motion Picture History
description: Using a world-building and storytelling framework similar to a table-top roleplaying game, students create characters that become vampires shortly after the invention of the photographic image. They come together as covens and witness the evolution of motion pictures through the present day, encountering media and culture spanning 200 years. The semester culminates in a festival of the history of images and motion pictures, recounting the unlife of images as it relates to living cultural histories.
prerequisites_raw: At least one 2000-Level course in COMM, GSAS, LITR, STSO, ARTS or WRIT

title: Readings in Literature Studies
description: Individual and collaborative projects and assignments adapted to the needs of individual students at the graduate level.
